manifest.title: Depth Hierarchies for Symmetric Algebraic Circuits

inputs.abstract:
Algebraic complexity studies the cost of computing families of polynomials by algebraic circuits, with the central goal of proving super-polynomial circuit lower bounds and separations between different models of algebraic computation. Since such lower bounds remain elusive for general circuits, a common strategy is to focus on restricted models. A recent line of work (ICALP 2020, ITCS & STOC 2026) introduces and studies symmetry as a syntactic circuit restriction, showing exponential symmetric lower bounds for the permanent, as well as separations between symmetric analogues of algebraic formulas ($\mathsf{symVF}$), skew circuits ($\mathsf{symVS}$), and circuits ($\mathsf{symVP}$).

Motivated by the progress of this research programme, we investigate the role of depth as a complexity parameter in symmetric circuits. For every fixed $\Delta \geq 1$, we exhibit a family of polynomials computable by symmetric circuits of polynomial size and depth $2\Delta+3$, but requiring size $n^{\Omega(\log n)}$ at depth $\Delta$. For a parameter called support depth, which captures the semantically relevant concept of depth for symmetric circuits, this complexity gap arises already between $\Delta$ and $\Delta+1$.

We also define symmetric versions of the bounded-depth algebraic complexity classes $\mathsf{VAC}^k$, for all $k \in \mathbb{N}$, that we call $\mathsf{symVAC}^k$, and establish two strict hierarchies: Firstly, a hierarchy within $\mathsf{symVAC}^0$, corresponding to constant-depth symmetric computation, and secondly, a hierarchy of the form $\mathsf{symVAC}^k \subsetneq \mathsf{symVAC}^{k+1}$ for all $k$. The latter shows that symmetric circuits of depth $(\log n)^{k+1}$ are strictly more powerful than depth-$(\log n)^k$ circuits. Our results are obtained via a graph-theoretic characterisation of the symmetric complexity classes in terms of homomorphism polynomials. This also allows us to place the bounded-depth classes within the landscape of symmetric algebraic complexity developed by Dwivedi, Pago and Seppelt (STOC 2026). Finally, we complement this picture by introducing $\mathsf{symVNP}$, a symmetric analogue of $\mathsf{VNP}$, and establishing $\mathsf{symVNP}$-completeness of the permanent under symmetric projections.

import Lax461425.SymmetricABPs
import Lax461425.PatternWidths

/-!
---
title: Symmetric ABPs for bounded-pathwidth patterns
type: theorem
---
For `n ≥ 1`, the homomorphism polynomial of a pattern of pathwidth at most `k` on `n × n`
matrices is computed by a matrix-symmetric ABP whose vertex orbits have size at most
`n^(k+1)`.
-/

namespace Lax461425.ABPsForPatterns

open SymmetricABPs HomomorphismPolynomials PatternWidths

/-- Homomorphism polynomials of patterns of pathwidth at most `k` have matrix-symmetric ABPs
with vertex orbits of size at most `n^(k+1)`. -/
axiom exists_abp {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {n k : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (F : Pattern) (hF : PathwidthLE k F) :
    ∃ G : ABP (Fin n × Fin n) K,
      G.Computes (hom K F n) ∧ G.IsMatrixSymmetric ∧ G.orbitSize ≤ n ^ (k + 1)

end Lax461425.ABPsForPatterns

concepts.title: Characterisation of bounded-depth matrix-symmetric circuits
concepts.description:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be a field of characteristic zero. Let $\Delta \geq 1$, $k \geq 2$, and
$n \geq 2k + 1$. For a polynomial $p \in \mathbb{K}[\mathcal{X}_n]$, the following are
equivalent:

1. $p$ is computed by a reduced matrix-symmetric circuit of support size $\leq k$ and support
   depth $\leq \Delta$.
2. $p$ is a linear combination of homomorphism polynomials $\hom_{F,n}$ for patterns $F$ with
   $\mathrm{fw}_\Delta(F) \leq k - 1$.

The implication from 1 to 2 is the theorem on homomorphism polynomials from symmetric
circuits. For the implication from 2 to 1, one constructs a circuit for every pattern in the
linear combination as in the theorem on circuits for patterns of bounded forestwidth,
multiplies the output gates by the coefficients, adds an output sum gate, and rigidifies.

import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Span.Defs
import Lax461425.Supports
import Lax461425.Forestwidth

/-!
---
title: Characterisation of bounded-depth matrix-symmetric circuits
type: theorem
---
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be a field of characteristic zero. Let $\Delta \geq 1$, $k \geq 2$, and
$n \geq 2k + 1$. For a polynomial $p \in \mathbb{K}[\mathcal{X}_n]$, the following are
equivalent:

1. $p$ is computed by a reduced matrix-symmetric circuit of support size $\leq k$ and support
   depth $\leq \Delta$.
2. $p$ is a linear combination of homomorphism polynomials $\hom_{F,n}$ for patterns $F$ with
   $\mathrm{fw}_\Delta(F) \leq k - 1$.

The implication from 1 to 2 is the theorem on homomorphism polynomials from symmetric
circuits. For the implication from 2 to 1, one constructs a circuit for every pattern in the
linear combination as in the theorem on circuits for patterns of bounded forestwidth,
multiplies the output gates by the coefficients, adds an output sum gate, and rigidifies.
-/

open Lax461425.SymmetricFamilies (MatrixPolynomial)

namespace Lax461425.BoundedDepthCharacterisation

open Circuits MatrixSymmetry Supports HomomorphismPolynomials Forestwidth

/-- A polynomial is computed by a reduced matrix-symmetric circuit of support size `≤ k` and
support depth `≤ Δ` if, and only if, it is a linear combination of homomorphism polynomials of
patterns of `Δ`-forestwidth at most `k - 1`. -/
axiom characterisation {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K] {Δ k n : ℕ} (hΔ : 1 ≤ Δ)
    (hk : 2 ≤ k) (hn : 2 * k + 1 ≤ n) (p : MatrixPolynomial n K) :
    (∃ C : Circuit (Fin n × Fin n) K,
        C.Computes p ∧ C.IsReduced ∧ IsMatrixSymmetric C ∧
          supportSize C ≤ k ∧ supportDepth C ≤ Δ) ↔
      p ∈ Submodule.span K {q | ∃ F : Pattern, ForestwidthLE Δ (k - 1) F ∧ hom K F n = q}

end Lax461425.BoundedDepthCharacterisation

              (Submodule.span K

                  Exists fun F =>
                    And (Lax461425.Forestwidth.ForestwidthLE Δ (instHSub.hSub k 1) F)
                      (Eq (Lax461425.HomomorphismPolynomials.hom K F n) q)))
              p)

concepts.description: Additional predicates on the existing circuit data.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax461425.Circuits

/-!
---
title: Formula and skew circuit properties
type: definition
---
Additional predicates on the existing circuit data.
-/

namespace Lax461425.CircuitProperties

open Circuits

open scoped Classical

/-- A formula has no parallel wires and may share inputs, while each noninput gate has
at most one outgoing wire. -/
def IsFormula {V K : Type*} (C : Circuit V K) : Prop :=
  (∀ g h, C.wire g h ≤ 1) ∧
    ∀ g, ¬ (C.label g).IsInput → ∑ h, C.wire h g ≤ 1

/-- At most one incoming wire of a product gate comes from a noninput gate. -/
def IsSkew {V K : Type*} (C : Circuit V K) : Prop :=
  ∀ g, C.label g = .mul → ∑ h, (if (C.label h).IsInput then 0 else C.wire g h) ≤ 1

end Lax461425.CircuitProperties

concepts.title: Algebraic circuits
concepts.description:
An *algebraic circuit* over a commutative ring $\mathbb{K}$ with variables from a set $V$ is a
finite directed acyclic graph whose input gates are labelled by variables or constants of
$\mathbb{K}$ and whose internal gates are labelled by $+$ or $\times$. We allow unbounded fan-in
and parallel wires: the number of wires from a gate $h$ to a gate $g$ is the *multiplicity*
$m(g,h) \in \mathbb{N}$, and $h$ is a *child* of $g$ if $m(g,h) > 0$. Input gates have no
children. There is a distinguished output gate, and every gate lies on a path to it.

Every gate $g$ computes a polynomial $p_g \in \mathbb{K}[V]$: an input gate computes its label,
and
$$
  p_g = \sum_h m(g,h)\, p_h \quad\text{or}\quad p_g = \prod_h p_h^{m(g,h)}
$$
if $g$ is a sum or a product gate, respectively, so that wires are counted with multiplicity
and empty sums and products are $0$ and $1$. The circuit *computes* the polynomial of its
output gate. Formally, "the gate $g$ computes $p$" is defined inductively by these rules, so
that exactly the polynomials obtained by evaluating the circuit bottom-up are computed. Every
gate computes exactly one polynomial; the values $p_h$ at children $h$ with $m(g,h) = 0$ do not
contribute.

The *size* of a circuit is the number of its gates and wires, counting multiplicities. A
*path* of length $m$ is a sequence of gates $g_0, \dots, g_m$ such that $g_{i+1}$ is a child of
$g_i$ for all $i < m$. The *depth* is the maximum length of a path. Since every gate lies on a
path to the output gate, this is the maximum number of wires on a path from the output gate to
a gate without children, e.g. an input gate.

A circuit is *reduced* if no two distinct input gates have the same label and no two distinct
internal gates have the same label and the same multiset of children, i.e. the same
multiplicities $m(g, \cdot)$.

import Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card
import Mathlib.Logic.Relation

/-!
---
title: Algebraic circuits
type: definition
---
An *algebraic circuit* over a commutative ring $\mathbb{K}$ with variables from a set $V$ is a
finite directed acyclic graph whose input gates are labelled by variables or constants of
$\mathbb{K}$ and whose internal gates are labelled by $+$ or $\times$. We allow unbounded fan-in
and parallel wires: the number of wires from a gate $h$ to a gate $g$ is the *multiplicity*
$m(g,h) \in \mathbb{N}$, and $h$ is a *child* of $g$ if $m(g,h) > 0$. Input gates have no
children. There is a distinguished output gate, and every gate lies on a path to it.

Every gate $g$ computes a polynomial $p_g \in \mathbb{K}[V]$: an input gate computes its label,
and
$$
  p_g = \sum_h m(g,h)\, p_h \quad\text{or}\quad p_g = \prod_h p_h^{m(g,h)}
$$
if $g$ is a sum or a product gate, respectively, so that wires are counted with multiplicity
and empty sums and products are $0$ and $1$. The circuit *computes* the polynomial of its
output gate. Formally, "the gate $g$ computes $p$" is defined inductively by these rules, so
that exactly the polynomials obtained by evaluating the circuit bottom-up are computed. Every
gate computes exactly one polynomial; the values $p_h$ at children $h$ with $m(g,h) = 0$ do not
contribute.

The *size* of a circuit is the number of its gates and wires, counting multiplicities. A
*path* of length $m$ is a sequence of gates $g_0, \dots, g_m$ such that $g_{i+1}$ is a child of
$g_i$ for all $i < m$. The *depth* is the maximum length of a path. Since every gate lies on a
path to the output gate, this is the maximum number of wires on a path from the output gate to
a gate without children, e.g. an input gate.

A circuit is *reduced* if no two distinct input gates have the same label and no two distinct
internal gates have the same label and the same multiset of children, i.e. the same
multiplicities $m(g, \cdot)$.
-/

namespace Lax461425.Circuits

/-- The label of a gate: a variable, a constant, or one of the operations `+` and `×`. -/
inductive GateLabel (V K : Type*) where
  | var (x : V)
  | const (c : K)
  | add
  | mul

namespace GateLabel

variable {V K : Type*}

/-- Input gates are the gates labelled by a variable or a constant. -/
def IsInput : GateLabel V K → Prop
  | var _ => True
  | const _ => True
  | add => False
  | mul => False

/-- Rename the variable of a label along `π`, keeping constants and operations fixed. -/
def map (π : V → V) : GateLabel V K → GateLabel V K
  | var x => var (π x)
  | const c => const c
  | add => add
  | mul => mul

end GateLabel

/-- An algebraic circuit with variables `V` and constants from `K`. -/
structure Circuit (V K : Type*) where
  /-- The finite set of gates. -/
  Gate : Type
  [fintypeGate : Fintype Gate]
  /-- The label of each gate. -/
  label : Gate → GateLabel V K
  /-- `wire g h` is the multiplicity of the wire from `h` into `g`. -/
  wire : Gate → Gate → ℕ
  /-- The output gate. -/
  out : Gate
  /-- Input gates have no children. -/
  wire_eq_zero_of_isInput : ∀ g h, (label g).IsInput → wire g h = 0
  /-- There is no directed cycle. -/
  acyclic : ∀ g, ¬ Relation.TransGen (fun h g => 0 < wire g h) g g
  /-- Every gate lies on a path to the output gate. -/
  reaches_out : ∀ g, Relation.ReflTransGen (fun h g => 0 < wire g h) g out

attribute [instance] Circuit.fintypeGate

namespace Circuit

variable {V K : Type*} (C : Circuit V K)

/-- `C.ComputesAt g p`: the gate `g` computes the polynomial `p`. A sum or product gate
computes the sum or product of polynomials `q h` computed at its children `h`, counted with
multiplicity. -/
inductive ComputesAt [CommSemiring K] (C : Circuit V K) : C.Gate → MvPolynomial V K → Prop
  | var {g : C.Gate} {x : V} : C.label g = .var x → C.ComputesAt g (MvPolynomial.X x)
  | const {g : C.Gate} {c : K} : C.label g = .const c → C.ComputesAt g (MvPolynomial.C c)
  | add {g : C.Gate} (q : C.Gate → MvPolynomial V K) : C.label g = .add →
      (∀ h, 0 < C.wire g h → C.ComputesAt h (q h)) → C.ComputesAt g (∑ h, C.wire g h • q h)
  | mul {g : C.Gate} (q : C.Gate → MvPolynomial V K) : C.label g = .mul →
      (∀ h, 0 < C.wire g h → C.ComputesAt h (q h)) → C.ComputesAt g (∏ h, q h ^ C.wire g h)

/-- The circuit computes the polynomial `p` at its output gate. -/
def Computes [CommSemiring K] (p : MvPolynomial V K) : Prop :=
  C.ComputesAt C.out p

/-- The number of gates plus the number of wires, counted with multiplicity. -/
def size : ℕ :=
  Fintype.card C.Gate + ∑ g, ∑ h, C.wire g h

/-- The gates `p 0, …, p m` form a path: each `p (i + 1)` is a child of `p i`. -/
def IsPath {m : ℕ} (p : Fin (m + 1) → C.Gate) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : Fin m, 0 < C.wire (p i.castSucc) (p i.succ)

/-- The maximum length of a path. -/
noncomputable def depth : ℕ :=
  sSup {m | ∃ p : Fin (m + 1) → C.Gate, C.IsPath p}

/-- No two distinct input gates carry the same label, and no two distinct internal gates carry
the same label and the same multiset of children. -/
def IsReduced : Prop :=
  (∀ g g', (C.label g).IsInput → C.label g = C.label g' → g = g') ∧
    ∀ g g', ¬ (C.label g).IsInput → C.label g = C.label g' → C.wire g = C.wire g' → g = g'

end Circuit

end Lax461425.Circuits

import Lax461425.Supports
import Lax461425.Forestwidth

/-!
---
title: Circuits for patterns of bounded forestwidth
type: theorem
---
Let $\Delta \geq 1$, $k \geq 2$, and $n \geq 2k + 1$. Let $F$ be a pattern with
$\mathrm{fw}_\Delta(F) \leq k - 1$. Then $\hom_{F,n}$ is computed by a reduced
matrix-symmetric circuit of support size $\leq k$, support depth $\leq \Delta$, orbit size
$\leq n^k$, depth $\leq 2\Delta + 1$, and size $\leq 5 n^k (|V(F)| + |E(F)|) + 1$, where
$|E(F)|$ counts edges with multiplicity.
-/

namespace Lax461425.CircuitsForPatterns

open Circuits MatrixSymmetry Supports HomomorphismPolynomials Forestwidth

/-- The homomorphism polynomial of a pattern of `Δ`-forestwidth at most `k - 1` is computed by a
reduced matrix-symmetric circuit of support size `≤ k`, support depth `≤ Δ`, orbit size
`≤ n ^ k`, depth `≤ 2Δ + 1`, and size `≤ 5 n ^ k (|V(F)| + |E(F)|) + 1`. -/
axiom exists_circuit {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K] {Δ k n : ℕ} (hΔ : 1 ≤ Δ) (hk : 2 ≤ k)
    (hn : 2 * k + 1 ≤ n) (F : Pattern) (hF : ForestwidthLE Δ (k - 1) F) :
    ∃ C : Circuit (Fin n × Fin n) K,
      C.Computes (hom K F n) ∧ C.IsReduced ∧ IsMatrixSymmetric C ∧
        supportSize C ≤ k ∧
        supportDepth C ≤ Δ ∧
        orbitSize C ≤ n ^ k ∧
        C.depth ≤ 2 * Δ + 1 ∧
        C.size ≤ 5 * n ^ k * (Fintype.card F.A + Fintype.card F.B + ∑ a, ∑ b, F.mult a b) + 1

end Lax461425.CircuitsForPatterns

concepts.title: Symmetric depth hierarchy
concepts.description:
For $\Delta, n \geq 1$, let $T_{\Delta,n}$ denote the full $n$-ary tree of depth $\Delta$,
viewed as a pattern.

1. For $\Delta \geq 1$ and $n \geq 20$, every matrix-symmetric circuit of support depth
   $\leq \Delta$ computing $\hom_{T_{\Delta,n},n}$ has orbit size at least
   $$
     n^{\log_2 n - \Delta \log_2 \log_2 n - 3}.
   $$
2. For $\Delta \geq 1$ and $n \geq 5$, there is a matrix-symmetric circuit of support depth
   $\leq \Delta + 1$ and orbit size $\leq n^2$ computing $\hom_{T_{\Delta,n},n}$.

import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Base
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Finite.List
import Lax461425.Supports
import Lax461425.HomomorphismPolynomials

/-!
---
title: Symmetric depth hierarchy
type: theorem
---
For $\Delta, n \geq 1$, let $T_{\Delta,n}$ denote the full $n$-ary tree of depth $\Delta$,
viewed as a pattern.

1. For $\Delta \geq 1$ and $n \geq 20$, every matrix-symmetric circuit of support depth
   $\leq \Delta$ computing $\hom_{T_{\Delta,n},n}$ has orbit size at least
   $$
     n^{\log_2 n - \Delta \log_2 \log_2 n - 3}.
   $$
2. For $\Delta \geq 1$ and $n \geq 5$, there is a matrix-symmetric circuit of support depth
   $\leq \Delta + 1$ and orbit size $\leq n^2$ computing $\hom_{T_{\Delta,n},n}$.

-/

namespace Lax461425.DepthHierarchy

open Circuits MatrixSymmetry Supports HomomorphismPolynomials

/-- The words over `Fin n` of length at most `Δ` whose length satisfies `p`. -/
abbrev Words (Δ n : ℕ) (p : ℕ → Prop) : Type :=
  {w : List (Fin n) // w.length ≤ Δ ∧ p w.length}

instance (Δ n : ℕ) (p : ℕ → Prop) : Finite (Words Δ n p) :=
  ((List.finite_length_le (Fin n) Δ).subset fun _ hw => hw.1).to_subtype

/-- The full `n`-ary tree `T_{Δ,n}` of depth `Δ`: its vertices are the words over `Fin n` of
length at most `Δ`, words of even length on the left and of odd length on the right, and a word
`w` is adjacent to the words `w ++ [i]`. -/
noncomputable def fullTree (Δ n : ℕ) : Pattern where
  A := Words Δ n Even
  B := Words Δ n Odd
  fintypeA := Fintype.ofFinite _
  fintypeB := Fintype.ofFinite _
  decEqA := inferInstance
  decEqB := inferInstance
  mult a b := by
    classical
    exact if (∃ i, b.1 = a.1 ++ [i]) ∨ ∃ i, a.1 = b.1 ++ [i] then 1 else 0

/-- Every reduced matrix-symmetric circuit of support depth `≤ Δ` computing `hom_{T_{Δ,n},n}`
has orbit size at least `n ^ (log₂ n - Δ log₂ log₂ n - 3)`. -/
axiom orbitSize_ge {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K] {Δ n : ℕ} (hΔ : 1 ≤ Δ) (hn : 20 ≤ n)
    (C : Circuit (Fin n × Fin n) K) (hC : C.Computes (hom K (fullTree Δ n) n))
    (hred : C.IsReduced) (hsym : IsMatrixSymmetric C) (hdepth : supportDepth C ≤ Δ) :
    (n : ℝ) ^ (Real.logb 2 n - Δ * Real.logb 2 (Real.logb 2 n) - 3) ≤ orbitSize C

/-- `hom_{T_{Δ,n},n}` is computed by a reduced matrix-symmetric circuit of support depth
`≤ Δ + 1` and orbit size `≤ n ^ 2`. -/
axiom exists_circuit {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K] {Δ n : ℕ} (hΔ : 1 ≤ Δ) (hn : 5 ≤ n) :
    ∃ C : Circuit (Fin n × Fin n) K,
      C.Computes (hom K (fullTree Δ n) n) ∧ C.IsReduced ∧ IsMatrixSymmetric C ∧
        supportDepth C ≤ Δ + 1 ∧ orbitSize C ≤ n ^ 2

end Lax461425.DepthHierarchy

concepts.title: Δ-forestwidth
concepts.description:
A *tree decomposition* of a graph $F$ is a tree $T$ with bags $\beta(t) \subseteq V(F)$ for
$t \in V(T)$ such that every vertex of $F$ lies in some bag, both endpoints of every edge lie
in a common bag, and, for every vertex $v$ of $F$, the nodes whose bags contain $v$ induce a
connected subtree of $T$. Edge multiplicities play no role.

Let $\Delta \geq 1$. The *$\Delta$-forestwidth* $\mathrm{fw}_\Delta(F)$ of $F$ is the least
$w \geq 0$ such that $F$ admits a tree decomposition $(T, \beta)$ with root $r$ such that $T$
has depth at most $\Delta$, $\beta(r) = \emptyset$, and $|\beta(t)| \leq w + 1$ for all
$t \in V(T)$. Equivalently, deleting $r$ yields a forest decomposition of $F$ in which every
root-leaf path has at most $\Delta$ nodes. This is a modification of the $\Delta$-treewidth,
for which this forest decomposition is required to be a tree decomposition.

We formalise the statement $\mathrm{fw}_\Delta(F) \leq w$ as the existence of such a
decomposition. A rooted tree of depth at most $\Delta$ is given by its finite set of nodes,
its root $r$, and the parent map, extended by $\mathrm{parent}(r) = r$, such that
$\mathrm{parent}^\Delta(t) = r$ for every node $t$. In such a tree, a set $U$ of nodes induces
a connected subtree if, and only if, at most one node $t \in U$ is the root or has its parent
outside $U$. As the root bag is empty, it suffices to require for every vertex $v$ that at
most one node $t$ has $v \in \beta(t)$ and $v \notin \beta(\mathrm{parent}(t))$.

open HomomorphismPolynomials

/-- A tree decomposition of the pattern `F` whose tree has depth at most `Δ` and an empty root
bag, and whose bags have at most `k` elements. -/
structure DepthDecomposition (F : Pattern) (Δ k : ℕ) where
  /-- The nodes of the tree. -/
  Node : Type
  [fintypeNode : Fintype Node]
  /-- The root of the tree. -/
  root : Node
  /-- The parent of each node; the root is its own parent. -/
  parent : Node → Node
  parent_root : parent root = root
  /-- Every node is at distance at most `Δ` from the root. -/
  depth_le : ∀ t, parent^[Δ] t = root
  /-- The bag of each node. -/
  bag : Node → Finset (F.A ⊕ F.B)
  bag_root : bag root = ∅
  card_bag_le : ∀ t, (bag t).card ≤ k
  /-- Every vertex lies in some bag. -/
  exists_mem_bag : ∀ v, ∃ t, v ∈ bag t
  /-- Both endpoints of every edge lie in a common bag. -/
  exists_edge_mem_bag : ∀ a b, F.mult a b ≠ 0 → ∃ t, Sum.inl a ∈ bag t ∧ Sum.inr b ∈ bag t
  /-- The nodes whose bags contain a vertex `v` induce a connected subtree: at most one of
  them has a parent whose bag does not contain `v`. -/
  connected : ∀ v t t', v ∈ bag t → v ∉ bag (parent t) → v ∈ bag t' → v ∉ bag (parent t') →
    t = t'

attribute [instance] DepthDecomposition.fintypeNode

/-- `fw_Δ(F) ≤ w`: the pattern `F` has a tree decomposition of depth at most `Δ` with empty
root bag and bags of size at most `w + 1`. -/
def ForestwidthLE (Δ w : ℕ) (F : Pattern) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (DepthDecomposition F Δ (w + 1))

end Lax461425.Forestwidth

concepts.title: Symmetric formulas for patterns of bounded treedepth
concepts.description:
Over a field of characteristic zero, for $n \geq 1$ and every pattern $F$ of treedepth at most
$t$, the homomorphism polynomial $\hom_{F,n}$ is computed by a matrix-symmetric formula of
orbit size at most $n^{t+2}$.

For an elimination forest of height at most $t$, the formula has a sum gate for every vertex
$v$ and every assignment of values in $[n]$ to the proper ancestors of $v$. It sums over the
values of $v$ the product of the edge variables from $v$ to its ancestors and of the sum gates
of the children of $v$. Parallel edges are multiplied out one at a time. Each copy of a
subformula is multiplied by its own pair of mutually inverse constants, which are chosen
distinct and different from all other constants, so that automorphisms cannot exchange copies.
Hence every internal gate lies in an orbit of size at most $n^t$, and input gates lie in orbits
of size at most $n^2$.

concepts.title: Support depth of symmetric formulas
concepts.description:
Let $n \geq 20$ and $\kappa \in \mathbb{N}$ with $3\kappa \leq n + 2$. Every polynomial
computed by a matrix-symmetric formula of orbit size $< \binom{n}{\kappa}$ is computed by a
reduced matrix-symmetric circuit of support size $\leq \kappa - 1$ and support depth
$\leq 2\kappa$.

The circuit is the rigidification of the formula, whose support size is bounded by the support
theorem. In a formula, every internal gate has a unique chain of ancestors. A path in the
rigidification with many support-changing wires can be moved by stabilisers so that each such
wire adds a new point to the union of the supports along the path. Lifting the path to the
formula, the gates at its end lie in a gate orbit at least as large as the orbit of this union,
which bounds the number of support-changing wires.

concepts.title: Homomorphism polynomials
concepts.description:
A *pattern* is a finite bipartite multigraph $F$ with a fixed bipartition $A \uplus B$, where
parallel edges are allowed. It is given by the multiplicity $F(a, b) \in \mathbb{N}$ of the
edge $ab$ for all $a \in A$ and $b \in B$. Its vertex set is $V(F) = A \uplus B$, and its edges
are the pairs $ab$ with $F(a,b) > 0$. The *underlying simple graph* of $F$ has vertex set
$A \uplus B$, with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$ adjacent if $F(a, b) > 0$. For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the *homomorphism polynomial* of
$F$ is
$$
  \hom_{F,n} = \sum_{\substack{h_A \colon A \to [n] \\ h_B \colon B \to [n]}}
    \prod_{ab \in E(F)} x_{h_A(a), h_B(b)} \in \mathbb{K}[\mathcal{X}_n],
$$
where the product counts edges with multiplicity. On the bi-adjacency matrix of a bipartite
graph, it counts the homomorphisms respecting the bipartitions.

    \prod_{ab \in E(F)} x_{h_A(a), h_B(b)} \in \mathbb{K}[\mathcal{X}_n],
$$
where the product counts edges with multiplicity. On the bi-adjacency matrix of a bipartite
graph, it counts the homomorphisms respecting the bipartitions.
-/

open Lax461425.SymmetricFamilies (MatrixPolynomial)

namespace Lax461425.HomomorphismPolynomials

/-- A finite bipartite multigraph with bipartition `A ⊎ B`. -/
structure Pattern where
  /-- The left side of the bipartition. -/
  A : Type
  /-- The right side of the bipartition. -/
  B : Type
  [fintypeA : Fintype A]
  [decEqA : DecidableEq A]
  [fintypeB : Fintype B]
  [decEqB : DecidableEq B]
  /-- `mult a b` is the number of edges between `a` and `b`. -/
  mult : A → B → ℕ

attribute [instance] Pattern.fintypeA Pattern.decEqA Pattern.fintypeB Pattern.decEqB

/-- The underlying simple graph of a pattern: `a` and `b` are adjacent if `F.mult a b ≠ 0`. -/
def underlying (F : Pattern) : SimpleGraph (F.A ⊕ F.B) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel fun u v => ∃ a b, u = Sum.inl a ∧ v = Sum.inr b ∧ F.mult a b ≠ 0

/-- The homomorphism polynomial `hom_{F,n}` in the variables `x_{i,j}` for `i, j ∈ [n]`. -/
noncomputable def hom (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (F : Pattern) (n : ℕ) :
    MatrixPolynomial n K :=
  ∑ hA : F.A → Fin n, ∑ hB : F.B → Fin n, ∏ a, ∏ b, MvPolynomial.X (hA a, hB b) ^ F.mult a b

end Lax461425.HomomorphismPolynomials

concepts.title: Matrix-symmetric circuits
concepts.description:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{X}_n = \{x_{i,j} : i, j \in [n]\}$ be the entries of an
$n \times n$ matrix of variables. The group $\Gamma_n = \mathbf{Sym}_n \times \mathbf{Sym}_n$
acts on $\mathcal{X}_n$ by permuting rows and columns independently,
$(\sigma, \tau)\, x_{i,j} = x_{\sigma(i), \tau(j)}$, and on the disjoint union
$[n] \uplus [n]$ of a copy of $[n]$ indexing the rows (the left side) and a copy indexing the
columns (the right side).

Let $C$ be an algebraic circuit with variables $\mathcal{X}_n$. A permutation $\sigma$ of the
gates of $C$ *extends* $\gamma \in \Gamma_n$ if it preserves the labels of internal gates and
the multiplicities of wires, $m(\sigma g, \sigma h) = m(g, h)$, and maps every input gate
labelled by a variable $x$ to a gate labelled by $\gamma x$ and every input gate labelled by a
constant to a gate labelled by the same constant. Such permutations are the circuit
automorphisms extending $\gamma$.

The circuit $C$ is *matrix-symmetric* if every $\gamma \in \Gamma_n$ extends to a circuit
automorphism, and *rigid* if every $\gamma \in \Gamma_n$ extends to a unique circuit
automorphism. Let $\mathbf{Aut}_\Gamma(C)$ be the group of circuit automorphisms extending
some element of $\Gamma_n$. The *orbit size* of $C$ is
$$
  \max_{g} \bigl|\{\sigma(g) : \sigma \in \mathbf{Aut}_\Gamma(C)\}\bigr|,
$$
the maximum taken over all gates $g$ of $C$.

columns (the right side).

Let $C$ be an algebraic circuit with variables $\mathcal{X}_n$. A permutation $\sigma$ of the
gates of $C$ *extends* $\gamma \in \Gamma_n$ if it preserves the labels of internal gates and
the multiplicities of wires, $m(\sigma g, \sigma h) = m(g, h)$, and maps every input gate
labelled by a variable $x$ to a gate labelled by $\gamma x$ and every input gate labelled by a
constant to a gate labelled by the same constant. Such permutations are the circuit
automorphisms extending $\gamma$.

The circuit $C$ is *matrix-symmetric* if every $\gamma \in \Gamma_n$ extends to a circuit
automorphism, and *rigid* if every $\gamma \in \Gamma_n$ extends to a unique circuit
automorphism. Let $\mathbf{Aut}_\Gamma(C)$ be the group of circuit automorphisms extending
some element of $\Gamma_n$. The *orbit size* of $C$ is
$$
  \max_{g} \bigl|\{\sigma(g) : \sigma \in \mathbf{Aut}_\Gamma(C)\}\bigr|,
$$
the maximum taken over all gates $g$ of $C$.
-/

namespace Lax461425.MatrixSymmetry

open Circuits

/-- The group `Γₙ = Symₙ × Symₙ` permuting rows and columns. -/
abbrev Γ (n : ℕ) := Equiv.Perm (Fin n) × Equiv.Perm (Fin n)

/-- The action of `Γₙ` on the variables: `(σ, τ) x_{i,j} = x_{σ(i), τ(j)}`. -/
def actVar {n : ℕ} (γ : Γ n) (x : Fin n × Fin n) : Fin n × Fin n :=
  (γ.1 x.1, γ.2 x.2)

/-- The action of `Γₙ` on `[n] ⊎ [n]`: rows on the left, columns on the right. -/
def actPoint {n : ℕ} (γ : Γ n) : Fin n ⊕ Fin n → Fin n ⊕ Fin n :=
  Sum.map γ.1 γ.2

variable {V K : Type*}

/-- The permutation `σ` of the gates is a circuit automorphism extending the renaming `π` of
the variables. -/
def Extends (C : Circuit V K) (σ : C.Gate ≃ C.Gate) (π : V → V) : Prop :=
  (∀ g, C.label (σ g) = (C.label g).map π) ∧ ∀ g h, C.wire (σ g) (σ h) = C.wire g h

variable {n : ℕ} (C : Circuit (Fin n × Fin n) K)

/-- Every element of `Γₙ` extends to a circuit automorphism. -/
def IsMatrixSymmetric : Prop :=
  ∀ γ : Γ n, ∃ σ : C.Gate ≃ C.Gate, Extends C σ (actVar γ)

/-- Every element of `Γₙ` extends to a unique circuit automorphism. -/
def IsRigid : Prop :=
  ∀ γ : Γ n, ∃! σ : C.Gate ≃ C.Gate, Extends C σ (actVar γ)

/-- The orbit of a gate under the circuit automorphisms extending elements of `Γₙ`. -/
def orbit (g : C.Gate) : Set C.Gate :=
  {g' | ∃ (γ : Γ n) (σ : C.Gate ≃ C.Gate), Extends C σ (actVar γ) ∧ σ g = g'}

/-- The maximum size of an orbit of a gate. -/
noncomputable def orbitSize : ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.sup fun g => (orbit C g).ncard

end Lax461425.MatrixSymmetry

concepts.title: Homomorphism polynomials outside the span of a graph class
concepts.description:
A pattern $F$ belongs to a class $\mathcal{F}$ of finite simple graphs if its underlying
simple graph does. For a graph $G$, let $\gamma(G) = \sum_{v \in V(G)} 2^{\deg_G(v) - 1}$, the number of vertices of a CFI

simple graphs that contains $K_1$, is minor-closed, and is closed under weak oddomorphisms.

concepts.title: Oddomorphisms
concepts.description:
Let $F$ and $G$ be graphs and $\varphi \colon F \to G$ a homomorphism. A vertex
$a \in V(F)$ is *$\varphi$-even* if $|N_F(a) \cap \varphi^{-1}(x)|$ is even for every
$x \in N_G(\varphi(a))$, and *$\varphi$-odd* if it is odd for every such $x$. The homomorphism
$\varphi$ is an *oddomorphism* if

1. every vertex $a \in V(F)$ is $\varphi$-even or $\varphi$-odd, and
2. for every $x \in V(G)$, the fibre $\varphi^{-1}(x)$ contains an odd number of $\varphi$-odd
   vertices.

The homomorphism $\varphi$ is a *weak oddomorphism* if there is a subgraph $F' \subseteq F$ such
that the restriction $\varphi|_{F'} \colon F' \to G$ is an oddomorphism. These notions are due
to Roberson.

A class $\mathcal{F}$ of finite simple graphs is *closed under weak oddomorphisms* if
$G \in \mathcal{F}$ whenever $F \in \mathcal{F}$ and there is a weak oddomorphism
$F \to G$.

import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Maps
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Subgraph
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card
import Lax871432.GraphClasses

/-!
---
title: Oddomorphisms
type: definition
---
Let $F$ and $G$ be graphs and $\varphi \colon F \to G$ a homomorphism. A vertex
$a \in V(F)$ is *$\varphi$-even* if $|N_F(a) \cap \varphi^{-1}(x)|$ is even for every
$x \in N_G(\varphi(a))$, and *$\varphi$-odd* if it is odd for every such $x$. The homomorphism
$\varphi$ is an *oddomorphism* if

1. every vertex $a \in V(F)$ is $\varphi$-even or $\varphi$-odd, and
2. for every $x \in V(G)$, the fibre $\varphi^{-1}(x)$ contains an odd number of $\varphi$-odd
   vertices.

The homomorphism $\varphi$ is a *weak oddomorphism* if there is a subgraph $F' \subseteq F$ such
that the restriction $\varphi|_{F'} \colon F' \to G$ is an oddomorphism. These notions are due
to Roberson.

A class $\mathcal{F}$ of finite simple graphs is *closed under weak oddomorphisms* if
$G \in \mathcal{F}$ whenever $F \in \mathcal{F}$ and there is a weak oddomorphism
$F \to G$.
-/

namespace Lax461425.Oddomorphisms

open Lax871432.GraphClasses

variable {V W : Type*} {F : SimpleGraph V} {G : SimpleGraph W}

/-- The neighbours of `a` in `F` that `φ` maps to `x`, i.e. `N_F(a) ∩ φ⁻¹(x)`. -/
def neighborsOver (φ : F →g G) (a : V) (x : W) : Set V :=
  {b | F.Adj a b ∧ φ b = x}

/-- `a` is `φ`-even: it has an even number of neighbours over every neighbour of `φ a`. -/
def IsEven (φ : F →g G) (a : V) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, G.Adj (φ a) x → Even (neighborsOver φ a x).ncard

/-- `a` is `φ`-odd: it has an odd number of neighbours over every neighbour of `φ a`. -/
def IsOdd (φ : F →g G) (a : V) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, G.Adj (φ a) x → Odd (neighborsOver φ a x).ncard

/-- `φ` is an oddomorphism: every vertex is `φ`-even or `φ`-odd, and every fibre contains an
odd number of `φ`-odd vertices. -/
structure IsOddomorphism (φ : F →g G) : Prop where
  even_or_odd : ∀ a, IsEven φ a ∨ IsOdd φ a
  odd_card_fibre : ∀ x, Odd {a | φ a = x ∧ IsOdd φ a}.ncard

/-- `φ` is a weak oddomorphism: its restriction to some subgraph of `F` is an oddomorphism. -/
def IsWeakOddomorphism (φ : F →g G) : Prop :=
  ∃ F' : F.Subgraph, IsOddomorphism (φ.comp F'.hom)

/-- `𝓕` is closed under weak oddomorphisms: the target of a weak oddomorphism from a member
is a member. -/
def IsWeakOddomorphismClosed (𝓕 : GraphClass) : Prop :=
  ∀ {V W : Type} [Finite V] [Finite W] {F : SimpleGraph V} {G : SimpleGraph W} (φ : F →g G),
    IsWeakOddomorphism φ → 𝓕.Mem F → 𝓕.Mem G

end Lax461425.Oddomorphisms

concepts.title: Treewidth, pathwidth, and treedepth of patterns
concepts.description:
The treewidth, pathwidth, and treedepth of a pattern are those of its underlying simple graph,
so edge multiplicities play no role. A pattern has treewidth at most $k$ if it has a tree
decomposition whose bags have at most $k + 1$ vertices, and pathwidth at most $k$ if it has
such a decomposition whose tree is a path. It has treedepth at most $t$ if it has an
elimination forest in which every root-leaf path has at most $t$ vertices. The pattern without
vertices has treewidth, pathwidth, and treedepth zero.

type: definition

The treewidth, pathwidth, and treedepth of a pattern are those of its underlying simple graph,
so edge multiplicities play no role. A pattern has treewidth at most $k$ if it has a tree
decomposition whose bags have at most $k + 1$ vertices, and pathwidth at most $k$ if it has
such a decomposition whose tree is a path. It has treedepth at most $t$ if it has an
elimination forest in which every root-leaf path has at most $t$ vertices. The pattern without
vertices has treewidth, pathwidth, and treedepth zero.

namespace Lax461425.PatternWidths

open HomomorphismPolynomials

/-- The pattern has treewidth at most `k`: its underlying simple graph has a tree decomposition
with bags of size at most `k + 1`. -/
def TreewidthLE (k : ℕ) (F : Pattern) : Prop :=
  Lax228581.Treewidth.HasTreewidthAtMost (underlying F) k

/-- The pattern has pathwidth at most `k`: its underlying simple graph has a path

  Lax183560.Pathwidth.HasPathwidthAtMost (underlying F) k

/-- The pattern has treedepth at most `t`: its underlying simple graph lies in the closure of a
rooted forest in which every root-leaf path has at most `t` vertices. -/
def TreedepthLE (t : ℕ) (F : Pattern) : Prop :=
  Lax183560.TreeDepth.HasTreedepthAtMost (underlying F) t

end Lax461425.PatternWidths

concepts.description:
The permanent polynomial, affine linear polynomials, and symmetric affine projections of
permanents. The order of the projected permanent is unrestricted.

import Lax461425.SymmetricFamilies
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Permanent
import Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.Rename
import Lax461425.MatrixSymmetry

/-!
---
title: Permanent polynomials and symmetric projections
type: definition
---
The permanent polynomial, affine linear polynomials, and symmetric affine projections of
permanents. The order of the projected permanent is unrestricted.
-/

open Lax461425.SymmetricFamilies (MatrixPolynomial)

namespace Lax461425.Permanent

open MatrixSymmetry

/-- The permanent polynomial on an `n × n` variable matrix. -/
noncomputable def permanent (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (n : ℕ) :
    MatrixPolynomial n K :=
  Matrix.permanent (fun i j => MvPolynomial.X (i, j))

/-- An affine linear polynomial, given by a constant and finitely many variable coefficients. -/
def IsAffine {V K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] (p : MvPolynomial V K) : Prop :=
  ∃ (c : K) (s : Finset V) (a : V → K),
    p = MvPolynomial.C c + ∑ v ∈ s, MvPolynomial.C (a v) * MvPolynomial.X v

/-- A symmetric affine projection of a permanent, with no restriction on the source order.
The finite index type is nonempty, corresponding to source order at least one. -/
def IsSymmetricProjection {V G K : Type*} [Group G] [CommSemiring K]
    (ρ : G →* Equiv.Perm V) (p : MvPolynomial V K) : Prop :=
  ∃ (A : Type) (_ : Fintype A) (_ : DecidableEq A) (_ : Nonempty A)
      (M : Matrix A A (MvPolynomial V K)),
    p = Matrix.permanent M ∧ (∀ i j, IsAffine (M i j)) ∧
      ∀ γ, ∃ α β : Equiv.Perm A,
        ∀ i j, M (α i) (β j) = MvPolynomial.rename (ρ γ) (M i j)

end Lax461425.Permanent

concepts.title: Reduced circuits are rigid
concepts.description:
Every reduced matrix-symmetric circuit is rigid.

Two circuit automorphisms extending the same element of $\Gamma_n$ differ by a circuit
automorphism $\rho$ that fixes all input gates, since input labels are distinct. By induction
on the height, $\rho$ fixes every gate $g$: the gate $\rho(g)$ has the same label and the same
multiset of children as $g$, so $\rho(g) = g$ as $C$ is reduced.

import Lax461425.SymmetricFamilies
import Lax461425.MatrixSymmetry

/-!
---
title: Rigidification
type: lemma
---
For every matrix-symmetric circuit $C$, there is a reduced matrix-symmetric circuit $C'$
computing the same polynomial whose size, depth, and orbit size are at most those of $C$.
-/

open Lax461425.SymmetricFamilies (MatrixPolynomial)

namespace Lax461425.Rigidification

open Circuits MatrixSymmetry

/-- Every matrix-symmetric circuit can be replaced by a reduced matrix-symmetric circuit
computing the same polynomial, without increasing size, depth, or orbit size. -/
axiom exists_reduced {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {n : ℕ}
    (C : Circuit (Fin n × Fin n) K) (hsym : IsMatrixSymmetric C)
    {p : MatrixPolynomial n K} (hp : C.Computes p) :
    ∃ C' : Circuit (Fin n × Fin n) K,
      C'.IsReduced ∧ IsMatrixSymmetric C' ∧ C'.Computes p ∧
        C'.size ≤ C.size ∧ C'.depth ≤ C.depth ∧ orbitSize C' ≤ orbitSize C

end Lax461425.Rigidification

concepts.title: Supports and support depth
concepts.description:
Let $C$ be a circuit with variables $\mathcal{X}_n$. For $S \subseteq [n] \uplus [n]$, let
$\mathbf{Stab}^\bullet(S) \leq \Gamma_n$ be the pointwise stabiliser of $S$. The set $S$
*supports* a gate $g$ if every circuit automorphism extending an element of
$\mathbf{Stab}^\bullet(S)$ fixes $g$. If $C$ is rigid, then $\Gamma_n$ acts on the gates of
$C$, and this says that $\mathbf{Stab}^\bullet(S)$ fixes $g$. The *support size* of $C$ is the
least $k$ such that every gate of $C$ has a support of size at most $k$.

Write $\sup(g)$ for the intersection of all supports of $g$ of size at most the support size
of $C$ — a bounded intersection: a support of unbounded size, such as the complement of a
single point, trivially has a trivial pointwise stabiliser and so carries no information about
$g$. If $g$ has a support $S$ with $|S_L|, |S_R| < n/2$, where $S_L$ and $S_R$ are the two
sides of $S$, then $\sup(g)$ is itself a support of $g$, the unique minimal one. A wire from
$h$ to $g$ is *support-changing* if $\sup(h) \not\subseteq \sup(g)$. If the support size of $C$
is less than $n/2$, the *support depth* of $C$ is the maximum number of support-changing wires
on a path. Otherwise, the support depth of $C$ is its depth. In either case, the support depth
is at most the depth.

/-!

title: Supports and support depth
type: definition
---

sides of $S$, then $\sup(g)$ is itself a support of $g$, the unique minimal one. A wire from
$h$ to $g$ is *support-changing* if $\sup(h) \not\subseteq \sup(g)$. If the support size of $C$
is less than $n/2$, the *support depth* of $C$ is the maximum number of support-changing wires
on a path. Otherwise, the support depth of $C$ is its depth. In either case, the support depth
is at most the depth.
-/

namespace Lax461425.Supports

open Circuits MatrixSymmetry

variable {K : Type*} {n : ℕ} (C : Circuit (Fin n × Fin n) K)

/-- `S` supports `g`: every circuit automorphism extending an element of `Γₙ` that fixes `S`
pointwise fixes `g`. -/
def IsSupport (g : C.Gate) (S : Set (Fin n ⊕ Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (γ : Γ n) (σ : C.Gate ≃ C.Gate), (∀ x ∈ S, actPoint γ x = x) → Extends C σ (actVar γ) → σ g = g

/-- The least `k` such that every gate has a support of size at most `k`. -/
noncomputable def supportSize : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | ∀ g, ∃ S, IsSupport C g S ∧ S.ncard ≤ k}

/-- `sup(g)`, the intersection of all supports of `g` of size at most `supportSize C`. Supports
of unbounded size are excluded: e.g. the complement of a single point always has a trivial
pointwise stabiliser, hence trivially supports every gate, and intersecting with it would
collapse `sup(g)` to the empty set regardless of `g`. -/
def minSupport (g : C.Gate) : Set (Fin n ⊕ Fin n) :=
  {x | ∀ S, IsSupport C g S → S.ncard ≤ supportSize C → x ∈ S}

/-- The number of support-changing wires on the path `p 0, …, p m`. -/
noncomputable def supportChanges {m : ℕ} (p : Fin (m + 1) → C.Gate) : ℕ :=
  {i : Fin m | ¬ minSupport C (p i.succ) ⊆ minSupport C (p i.castSucc)}.ncard

/-- The maximum number of support-changing wires on a path if the support size is less than
`n / 2`, and the depth otherwise. -/
noncomputable def supportDepth : ℕ :=
  if 2 * supportSize C < n then
    sSup {c | ∃ (m : ℕ) (p : Fin (m + 1) → C.Gate), C.IsPath p ∧ supportChanges C p = c}
  else
    C.depth

end Lax461425.Supports

concepts.title: Support theorem
concepts.description:
Let $n \geq 20$ and $\kappa \in \mathbb{N}$ with $3\kappa \leq n + 2$. Then every gate of a
reduced matrix-symmetric circuit of orbit size $< \binom{n}{\kappa}$ has a support of size
$\leq \kappa - 1$, i.e. the circuit has support size $\leq \kappa - 1$.

In the paper, the orbit size is bounded by a function $f \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$,
and $\kappa_f(n) = \min\{r \in \mathbb{N} : \binom{n}{r} > f(n)\}$. The statement there is
that, if $n \geq 20$ and $3\kappa_f(n) \leq n + 2$, every gate of a reduced matrix-symmetric
circuit of orbit size $\leq f(n)$ has a minimal support of size $\leq \kappa_f(n) - 1$. This
is the case $\kappa = \kappa_f(n)$ of the statement above. Conversely, the statement above for
any $\kappa$ follows from the paper's for the constant function $f$ with value the orbit size,
since then $\kappa_f(n) \leq \kappa$. As $2(\kappa - 1) < n$, the minimal supports exist and
are contained in every support of size $\leq \kappa - 1$, so bounding the support size is the
same as bounding the size of the minimal supports.

concepts.title: Symmetric algebraic branching programs
concepts.description:
An algebraic branching program (ABP) is a finite simple directed acyclic graph with
affine edge labels, a unique source and a unique sink; it computes the sum over all
source-to-sink paths of the product of the edge labels. An ABP in matrix variables is
matrix-symmetric if every row and column permutation extends to an ABP automorphism, and
its vertex orbits range over all such extending automorphisms. `symVBP` is the class of
families computed by matrix-symmetric ABPs with polynomial vertex orbits.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax461425.MatrixSymmetry
import Lax461425.SymmetricFamilies
import Lax461425.SymmetricClasses
import Lax461425.SymmetricVNP
import Lax461425.HomomorphismPolynomials
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Span.Defs
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Pi
import Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.Rename

/-!
---
title: Symmetric algebraic branching programs
type: definition
---
An algebraic branching program (ABP) is a finite simple directed acyclic graph with
affine edge labels, a unique source and a unique sink; it computes the sum over all
source-to-sink paths of the product of the edge labels. An ABP in matrix variables is
matrix-symmetric if every row and column permutation extends to an ABP automorphism, and
its vertex orbits range over all such extending automorphisms. `symVBP` is the class of
families computed by matrix-symmetric ABPs with polynomial vertex orbits.
-/

namespace Lax461425.SymmetricABPs

open Circuits MatrixSymmetry HomomorphismPolynomials

/-- An affine linear form, with an explicit coefficient for every variable. -/
structure AffineForm (V K : Type*) where
  constant : K
  coeff : V → K

/-- The polynomial represented by an affine form. -/
noncomputable def AffineForm.polynomial {V K : Type*} [Fintype V] [CommSemiring K]
    (a : AffineForm V K) : MvPolynomial V K :=
  MvPolynomial.C a.constant + ∑ x, MvPolynomial.C (a.coeff x) * MvPolynomial.X x

/-- A finite directed acyclic ABP. Every vertex occurs on a source-to-sink path. -/
structure ABP (V K : Type*) where
  Vertex : Type
  [fintypeVertex : Fintype Vertex]
  [decEqVertex : DecidableEq Vertex]
  edge : Vertex → Vertex → Prop
  [decEdge : DecidableRel edge]
  label : Vertex → Vertex → AffineForm V K
  source : Vertex
  sink : Vertex
  source_no_incoming : ∀ v, ¬ edge v source
  sink_no_outgoing : ∀ v, ¬ edge sink v
  acyclic : ∀ v, ¬ Relation.TransGen edge v v
  source_reaches : ∀ v, Relation.ReflTransGen edge source v
  reaches_sink : ∀ v, Relation.ReflTransGen edge v sink

attribute [instance] ABP.fintypeVertex ABP.decEqVertex ABP.decEdge

namespace ABP

variable {V K : Type*} (G : ABP V K)

/-- A bounded vertex sequence. Acyclic paths have fewer edges than there are vertices. -/
abbrev PathData := (l : Fin (Fintype.card G.Vertex)) × (Fin (l.val + 1) → G.Vertex)

/-- A vertex sequence traverses directed edges from the source to `v`. -/
def IsPathTo (v : G.Vertex) (p : G.PathData) : Prop :=
  p.2 0 = G.source ∧ p.2 (Fin.last p.1.val) = v ∧
    ∀ i : Fin p.1.val, G.edge (p.2 i.castSucc) (p.2 i.succ)

/-- All directed paths from the source to a specified vertex. -/
abbrev PathTo (v : G.Vertex) := {p : G.PathData // G.IsPathTo v p}

/-- A vertex sequence traverses directed edges from the source to the sink. -/
abbrev IsPath := G.IsPathTo G.sink

/-- All source-to-sink paths, including the empty path when source and sink coincide. -/
abbrev Path := G.PathTo G.sink

noncomputable instance (v : G.Vertex) : Fintype (G.PathTo v) := Fintype.ofFinite _

/-- The product of the labels along a path with any endpoint. -/
noncomputable def pathWeightTo [Fintype V] [CommSemiring K] {v : G.Vertex}
    (p : G.PathTo v) : MvPolynomial V K :=
  ∏ i : Fin p.1.1.val,
    (G.label (p.1.2 i.castSucc) (p.1.2 i.succ)).polynomial

/-- The product of the labels along a source-to-sink path. -/
noncomputable def pathWeight [Fintype V] [CommSemiring K] (p : G.Path) : MvPolynomial V K :=
  G.pathWeightTo p

/-- The sum of all source-to-`v` path weights. -/
noncomputable def polynomialAt [Fintype V] [CommSemiring K] (v : G.Vertex) :
    MvPolynomial V K := ∑ p : G.PathTo v, G.pathWeightTo p

/-- The sum of the weights of all source-to-sink paths. -/
noncomputable def polynomial [Fintype V] [CommSemiring K] : MvPolynomial V K :=
  G.polynomialAt G.sink

/-- The ABP computes the given polynomial. -/
def Computes [Fintype V] [CommSemiring K] (p : MvPolynomial V K) : Prop :=
  G.polynomial = p

/-- An ABP automorphism extending a renaming of the variables. Values of labels on
nonedges are immaterial. -/
def Extends [Fintype V] [CommSemiring K] (σ : G.Vertex ≃ G.Vertex) (π : V → V) : Prop :=
  σ G.source = G.source ∧ σ G.sink = G.sink ∧
    (∀ u v, G.edge (σ u) (σ v) ↔ G.edge u v) ∧
    ∀ u v, G.edge u v →
      (G.label (σ u) (σ v)).polynomial = MvPolynomial.rename π (G.label u v).polynomial

variable {n : ℕ} (G : ABP (Fin n × Fin n) K)

/-- Every matrix-variable permutation extends to an ABP automorphism. -/
def IsMatrixSymmetric [CommSemiring K] : Prop :=
  ∀ γ : Γ n, ∃ σ : G.Vertex ≃ G.Vertex, G.Extends σ (actVar γ)

/-- The vertex orbit under all extending ABP automorphisms. -/
def orbit [CommSemiring K] (v : G.Vertex) : Set G.Vertex :=
  {w | ∃ (γ : Γ n) (σ : G.Vertex ≃ G.Vertex), G.Extends σ (actVar γ) ∧ σ v = w}

/-- The largest vertex orbit under all extending ABP automorphisms. -/
noncomputable def orbitSize [CommSemiring K] : ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.sup fun v => (G.orbit v).ncard

end ABP

open SymmetricFamilies SymmetricClasses SymmetricVNP

/-- Families computed by matrix-symmetric ABPs of polynomial vertex-orbit size. No bound on
the total size or the degree is imposed. -/
def InSymVBP {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] (f : MatrixFamily K) : Prop :=
  ∃ b : ℕ → ℕ, PolynomiallyBounded b ∧ ∀ n, ∃ G : ABP (Fin n × Fin n) K,
    G.Computes (f n) ∧ G.IsMatrixSymmetric ∧ G.orbitSize ≤ b n

end Lax461425.SymmetricABPs

concepts.description:

Polynomial bounds allow a constant factor and use `n + 1`, including the zero-size matrix.

import Lax461425.CircuitProperties
import Lax461425.MatrixSymmetry
import Lax461425.SymmetricFamilies

open Lax461425.CircuitProperties

/-!
---
title: Symmetric complexity classes
type: definition
---
Families computed by matrix-symmetric circuits with polynomially bounded gate orbits.
Polynomial bounds allow a constant factor and use `n + 1`, including the zero-size matrix.
-/

namespace Lax461425.SymmetricClasses

open Circuits MatrixSymmetry SymmetricFamilies

/-- A polynomial bound, including finitely many exceptional indices. -/
def PolynomiallyBounded (q : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c d : ℕ, ∀ n, q n ≤ c * (n + 1) ^ d

/-- Polynomial gate-orbit witnesses satisfying an additional circuit property. -/
def InSymClass {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
    (P : ∀ n, Circuit (Fin n × Fin n) K → Prop) (f : MatrixFamily K) : Prop :=
  ∃ b : ℕ → ℕ, PolynomiallyBounded b ∧ ∀ n, ∃ C : Circuit (Fin n × Fin n) K,
    C.Computes (f n) ∧ IsMatrixSymmetric C ∧ MatrixSymmetry.orbitSize C ≤ b n ∧ P n C

/-- Symmetric polynomial-orbit circuits. No degree or total-size bound is imposed. -/
def InSymVP {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] (f : MatrixFamily K) : Prop :=
  InSymClass (fun _ _ => True) f

/-- Symmetric polynomial-orbit skew circuits. -/
def InSymVS {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] (f : MatrixFamily K) : Prop :=
  InSymClass (fun _ C => IsSkew C) f

/-- Symmetric polynomial-orbit formulas. -/
def InSymVF {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] (f : MatrixFamily K) : Prop :=
  InSymClass (fun _ C => IsFormula C) f

axiom formula_witness {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K] {n : ℕ}
    (hn : 1 ≤ n) (p : MatrixPolynomial n K) (hp : MatrixInvariant p) :
    ∃ (ρ : Γ n →* Equiv.Perm (Fin (2 * n ^ 2)))
      (g : MvPolynomial ((Fin n × Fin n) ⊕ Fin (2 * n ^ 2)) K)
      (C : Circuit ((Fin n × Fin n) ⊕ Fin (2 * n ^ 2)) K),
      C.Computes g ∧ Symmetric (jointAction ρ) C ∧
      orbitSize (jointAction ρ) C ≤ 4 * n ^ 2 ∧ IsFormula C ∧ boolSum g = p

concepts.description:

import Lax461425.CircuitProperties
import Lax461425.MatrixSymmetry
import Lax461425.SymmetricFamilies
import Lax461425.SymmetricClasses

open Lax461425.CircuitProperties

/-!
---
title: Symmetric VNP and hypercube-sum witnesses
type: definition
---
The symmetry and orbit definitions below allow a group to act jointly on matrix variables
and auxiliary variables. Orbits use every extending circuit automorphism. A family lies in
symmetric VNP if it is a sum over the Boolean hypercube of a polynomial computed by such a
jointly symmetric circuit with polynomial gate orbits.
-/

namespace Lax461425.SymmetricVNP

open Circuits MatrixSymmetry SymmetricFamilies SymmetricClasses
open scoped Classical

/-- The permutation action on matrix variables. -/
def matrixAction (n : ℕ) : Γ n →* Equiv.Perm (Fin n × Fin n) where
  toFun γ := Equiv.prodCongr γ.1 γ.2
  map_one' := rfl
  map_mul' _ _ := rfl

/-- The joint action on matrix and auxiliary variables. -/
def jointAction {n : ℕ} {Y : Type*} (ρ : Γ n →* Equiv.Perm Y) :
    Γ n →* Equiv.Perm ((Fin n × Fin n) ⊕ Y) where
  toFun γ := Equiv.sumCongr (matrixAction n γ) (ρ γ)
  map_one' := by ext x; cases x <;> simp [matrixAction]
  map_mul' γ δ := by ext x; cases x <;> simp [matrixAction]

/-- Sum over Boolean auxiliary assignments; distinct Booleans are counted separately even
in positive characteristic. -/
noncomputable def boolSum {X Y K : Type*} [Fintype Y] [CommSemiring K]
    (g : MvPolynomial (X ⊕ Y) K) : MvPolynomial X K :=
  ∑ e : Y → Bool, MvPolynomial.eval₂ MvPolynomial.C
    (Sum.elim MvPolynomial.X (fun y => MvPolynomial.C (if e y then 1 else 0))) g

/-- Every element of the acting group extends to a circuit automorphism. -/
def Symmetric {G V K : Type*} [Group G] (ρ : G →* Equiv.Perm V)
    (C : Circuit V K) : Prop :=
  ∀ γ : G, ∃ σ : C.Gate ≃ C.Gate, Extends C σ (ρ γ)

/-- Orbit under all automorphisms extending some element of the acting group. -/
def orbit {G V K : Type*} [Group G] (ρ : G →* Equiv.Perm V)
    (C : Circuit V K) (g : C.Gate) : Set C.Gate :=
  {g' | ∃ (γ : G) (σ : C.Gate ≃ C.Gate), Extends C σ (ρ γ) ∧ σ g = g'}

/-- The largest gate orbit for a specified variable action. -/
noncomputable def orbitSize {G V K : Type*} [Group G] (ρ : G →* Equiv.Perm V)
    (C : Circuit V K) : ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.sup fun g => (orbit ρ C g).ncard

/-- Hypercube-sum witnesses with polynomially many auxiliary variables and polynomial gate
orbits for the joint action. -/
def InHyperCubeSumClass {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
    (P : ∀ {V : Type}, Circuit V K → Prop) (f : MatrixFamily K) : Prop :=
  ∃ q b : ℕ → ℕ, PolynomiallyBounded q ∧ PolynomiallyBounded b ∧ ∀ n,
    ∃ (ρ : Γ n →* Equiv.Perm (Fin (q n)))
      (g : MvPolynomial ((Fin n × Fin n) ⊕ Fin (q n)) K)
      (C : Circuit ((Fin n × Fin n) ⊕ Fin (q n)) K),
      C.Computes g ∧ Symmetric (jointAction ρ) C ∧
      orbitSize (jointAction ρ) C ≤ b n ∧ P C ∧ boolSum g = f n

/-- The symmetric analogue of VNP. -/
def InSymVNP {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] (f : MatrixFamily K) : Prop :=
  InHyperCubeSumClass (fun _ => True) f

/-- The formula-witness variant of symmetric VNP. -/
def InSymVNPFormula {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] (f : MatrixFamily K) : Prop :=
  InHyperCubeSumClass (fun C => IsFormula C) f

end Lax461425.SymmetricVNP

proofs.description: Every polynomial in a symmetric VNP family is matrix-invariant.

The characterisation of bounded-depth matrix-symmetric circuits.

The forward direction (1 → 2) is the concept `PatternsFromCircuits.mem_span_hom` directly.

For the backward direction (2 → 1), `Submodule.mem_span_set'` writes `p = ∑ i, f i • hom K
(F i) n` for finitely many patterns `F i` with `ForestwidthLE Δ (k - 1) (F i)`. For each `i`, a
circuit `D i` computing `hom K (F i) n` is obtained from the concept
`CircuitsForPatterns.exists_circuit`; it is reduced, matrix-symmetric, with support size `≤ k`
and support depth `≤ Δ`. These are glued (`BoundedDepthGlueCircuit.glueCircuit`) by scaling each
block's output by `f i` (via a new `mul`-gate and a new `const (f i)` input gate) and summing
all of these via a new output `add`-gate; the glue circuit computes `∑ i, f i • hom K (F i) n =
p` (`BoundedDepthGlueComputes.glueCircuit_computes`) and is matrix-symmetric
(`BoundedDepthGlueSymmetric.glueCircuit_isMatrixSymmetric`), since every block is. Rigidifying
it (`RigidConstruction.reduced`) yields a reduced, matrix-symmetric circuit computing `p`
(`RigidReduced.isReduced_reduced`, `RigidSymmetric.isMatrixSymmetric_reduced`,
`RigidComputes.computes_transfer`) with support size `≤ k`
(`BoundedDepthGlueSize.glueCircuit_reduced_supportSize_le`) and support depth `≤ Δ`
(`BoundedDepthGlueSc.glueCircuit_reduced_supportDepth_le`), the latter via a potential built
from each block's own `sc`, since every glue gate has empty minimal support and every block's
own minimal support is unaffected by rigidifying the glue circuit as a whole
(`BoundedDepthEmbed.embed_equiv_eq`, `BoundedDepthReducedFormula.reduced_σOf_eq`).

The concept `Rigidification.exists_reduced` is deliberately not used: it does not preserve support
size or support depth, so the proof rigidifies with `RigidConstruction.reduced` and tracks the
supports of the block gates through it directly.

The tree `T_{Δ,n}` has a tree decomposition of depth `Δ + 1` with empty root bag and bags of
size `≤ 2` (`decomp`), so `CircuitsForPatterns.exists_circuit` with support size `2` applies.
By `choose_le_orbitSize` and the numerical estimate `arith`.

If `F` has an edge, after unfolding `ForestwidthLE Δ (k - 1) F` (the arithmetic
`(k - 1) + 1 = k`, using `k ≥ 2`, is immediate) into a `DepthDecomposition F Δ k`, we split on
whether `F` has isolated vertices (`isoJ F = 0` or not) and invoke
`exists_circuit_of_noIsolated` or `exists_circuit_of_isolated` respectively
(`exists_circuit_of_edge`). If `F` has no edges, `hom K F n` is the constant
`n ^ |F.A| * n ^ |F.B|` (`hom_eq_const_of_no_edge`), computed by the single-gate
`constCircuit`, of size `1`.

Non-uniform closure. Fix `v₀` and evaluate at the (padded) bi-adjacency matrices of the bipartite
double covers of the filled CFI graphs `Ĝ_0` and `Ĝ_{δ_{v₀}}`. Both evaluations agree on every
`hom_{F',N}` with `F' ∈ 𝓕` (`NU.minorLifting_eq`, using `NU.eval_hom`, `NU.homBip_pad`), hence on
`homSpan`, but differ on `hom_{F,N}` (`NU.minorLifting_lt`).

Partition the monomial support into distinct orbits. Each orbit sum is an embedding
polynomial divided by its nonzero automorphism factor; partition Möbius inversion
expresses it in the bounded-vertex homomorphism span, as in DPS, Lemma 4 and Corollary A.3.

**`mem_span_hom`.** A polynomial computed by a reduced matrix-symmetric circuit of support
size `≤ k` and support depth `≤ Δ` is a linear combination of homomorphism polynomials of
patterns of `Δ`-forestwidth at most `k - 1`.

Applies `PatternsInductionMain.exists_phi` (`lem:induction`) at `g := C.out`. Since
`minSupport C C.out = ∅` (`PatternsSupportBasic.minSupport_out`), `supOf hrig hn C.out = ∅` too
(`supOf_eq_minSupport`), so `leftCard hrig hn C.out = rightCard hrig hn C.out = 0`; the witness
`φ`, lifted from depth `sc C C.out` to `Δ` (`sc_le_supportDepth`, `hdepth`, `span𝔗P_mono`), is
evaluated at the (unique, since the arities are `0`) canonical enumerations, giving `p`
(`computesAt_unique`, since `C.Computes p` unfolds to `C.ComputesAt C.out p`). Every generator
`labelledHom K G n` of `span𝔗P K Δ k n (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 0 ⊕ Fin 0))`, evaluated at any
point, is exactly the *unlabelled* homomorphism polynomial `hom K G.F n`
(`labelledHom_eq_hom_of_zero`, since the defining `if`-condition of `labelledHom` is vacuously
true at arity `(0,0)`), and `G ∈ 𝒯^{Δ,k}(0,0)` is exactly `ForestwidthLE Δ (k - 1) G.F`
(`PatternsLabelledUnlabelled.inClass_ofPattern_iff`, using `G = ofPattern G.F` since both label
maps out of `Fin 0` are forced to be `Fin.elim0`); `eval_mem_span_hom` packages this as a
`Submodule.span_induction` argument, stated for an arbitrary arity `(ℓ, r)` with `ℓ = r = 0` as
*hypotheses* (rather than literal `Fin 0`s) so that it can be `subst`ed in directly against
`leftCard hrig hn C.out`/`rightCard hrig hn C.out`, with no further reindexing needed.

The permanent family has a polynomial-size jointly symmetric Boolean witness.
The result holds over every commutative ring, including characteristic two.
The hardness direction of Theorem 7.7, with unrestricted source order as in Definition 7.6.

Two circuit automorphisms extending the same element of `Γₙ` differ by an automorphism fixing
every input gate, since input labels are distinct; by induction on the child relation this
automorphism fixes every gate, using that `C` is reduced.

Given a matrix-symmetric circuit `C`, the circuit `C' := RigidConstruction.reduced C` is
obtained by merging gates that are equivalent under a height-indexed recursive equivalence
relation (`RigidEquiv.Equiv`): input gates are equivalent iff they share a label, and internal
gates of matching height and label are equivalent iff they send the same total wire weight,
aggregated by equivalence class (`RigidWeight.W`), into every class of smaller height. `C'`
keeps only the classes (canonical representatives chosen via `RigidRep.rep`) from which the
class of the output gate can still be reached. `C'` is reduced because distinct classes are
never merged (`RigidReduced.isReduced_reduced`); it computes the same polynomial because every

Rigidity (reducedness and matrix-symmetry) makes `Γₙ` act on the gates. The index of a gate
stabiliser is at most the orbit size, so by Dixon and Mortimer the stabiliser of every internal
gate contains the alternating group fixing fewer than `κ` points on each side; reducedness
upgrades it to the symmetric group, giving supports with sides of size `≤ κ - 1` by induction.
The `⊆`-least such support of a gate is mapped equivariantly by `Γₙ`, so its orbit is a lower
bound for the orbit of the gate; a binomial estimate then bounds its total size by `κ - 1`.

`symVF` consists of the families spanned by homomorphism polynomials of patterns of bounded
treedepth.

The homomorphism polynomial of a pattern of treedepth at most `t` has a matrix-symmetric
formula of orbit size at most `n ^ t ≤ n ^ (t + 2)`: sum gates over the values of the vertices
of an elimination forest, with tagged products of edge variables and child formulas.

The rigidification of a symmetric formula of orbit size `< n.choose κ` has support size
`≤ κ - 1` by the support theorem, and support depth `≤ 2κ`: along any path, support-changing
wires are moved by stabilisers so that each adds a new point to the union of supports; lifting
to the formula, where non-input gates have unique parents, bounds both sides of this union by
`κ - 1` while the path ends in a non-input gate.

`symVP` consists of the families spanned by homomorphism polynomials of patterns of bounded
treewidth. For large `n`, the support theorem bounds the support size of a rigidified circuit,
and the bounded-depth characterisation (with the support depth as depth bound) applies; for
the finitely many remaining `n`, matrix-invariance and the general homomorphism spanning theorem
suffice. Conversely, a common depth bound for the finitely many patterns in each linear
combination gives circuits via the bounded-depth characterisation, while finitely many
exceptional indices are covered by symmetric ABPs.

The nodes are the vertices below a new root; the parent of a vertex is its immediate
ancestor (the ancestor of largest rank), or the new root, and its bag consists of the vertex
and its ancestors. Bags are chains, so ranks are injective on them; ranks decrease towards
the root, so the depth is at most `t`. A vertex `v` leaves the bags exactly at the node `v`.

Each vertex is placed at its unique top node. Vertices at a node of depth `d` receive the ranks
`(d - 1)(w + 1), …, d(w + 1) - 1` in a fixed order, and `u` is an ancestor of `v` if it has
smaller rank and its top node is an ancestor of that of `v`. The endpoints of an edge lie in a
common bag, so their top nodes are both ancestors of that node, hence comparable.

Root the tree at any node `r`, take as parent the next node on the unique path to `r`, and add
a new root with an empty bag above `r`. A vertex has a unique top node because every node
containing it lies below each of its top nodes.

Joining every node to its parent gives a tree (connected, with one edge per non-root node),
and the nodes whose bags contain a vertex are connected to its unique top node.
